title: Credential adapter answer
description: What a credential adapter prints on its standard output, once, as one JSON document. An adapter is a program of the machine's, started by the runner outside the enclosure, that contains what one kind of host needs, such as a source code host: it mints or fetches a secret and defines how the secret is used, because hosts differ in that and the runner contains nothing specific to any host. It exits 0 with this document, or not 0 with a line on standard error.

token.description: The secret, for every apply entry that has none of its own.

expires_at.description: When the secret stops working, RFC 3339. The runner runs the adapter again five minutes before. Absent means it does not expire.

apply.description: Where the secret goes. Run again, an adapter returns the same hosts, schemes and paths: they are fixed when the run starts, and only the secret changes.

scheme.description: bearer sets Authorization: Bearer and the secret. basic sets Authorization: Basic with username and the secret as the password. header sets the header whose name is in header to the secret. The set is closed: an adapter chooses among what the runner implements.

paths.description: The paths of these hosts the run may request, the policy's path grammar; every other path of them is denied. Absent means every path.

placeholders.description: Variables the enclosure gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that needs one set to start: the proxy replaces what the program sends.
